whatItDoes: Exports PDF pages as JPEG images — one JPG per page — and packs them as a ZIP. Shows page count, creates 800×1120 placeholder JPGs with 'Page N of M' text, and allows download of individual JPGs or a ZIP of all pages. Client-side via pdf-lib and canvas.
whyItExists: Sharing PDF pages as images is handy for slides and previews, but uploading PDFs to a server risks privacy. This renders pages locally to JPEGs (currently placeholder rendering; full pdfjs-dist rasterization is planned) so your document never leaves the browser.
whoShouldUse: Anyone needing to turn PDF pages into images for presentations, thumbnails, or sharing where PDF viewers are not available.
useCases: Export a 10-page PDF as 10 JPGs and ZIP them for an image gallery
Create a thumbnail JPG of the first page for a document preview
instructions: Drop a PDF (10MB). The tool shows page count.
Click Export to JPG — each page is rendered to an 800×1120 JPEG (placeholder with page number) and a ZIP is prepared.
Download individual JPGs or the ZIP of all pages from the green card. All rendering is local.
examples: Input: 3-page PDF → Output: 3 JPGs (Page 1/3, 2/3, 3/3) + ZIP (~300KB total placeholder).
Input: 1-page PDF → Output: single JPG download.
bestPractices: For true rasterization, wait for pdfjs-dist integration; current placeholder is for layout testing
Use PDF Compressor first if the PDF is large before exporting to JPG
commonMistakes: Expecting pixel-perfect rendering — current version uses placeholder canvases; verify output before sharing
Uploading encrypted PDFs — they will error; decrypt first
faq: Is the PDF uploaded? No — export is pdf-lib + canvas in your browser. Files never leave your device.
Does it need pdfjs-dist? Full rasterization will use pdfjs-dist; currently a placeholder is used to keep the build light (no new dep).
Can I choose PNG? Currently JPEG only; PNG/WebP options are planned.
features: PDF → JPG, one per page, ZIP packed
